'''''Juniperus thurifera''''', Is a species of [[juniper]] native to the [[mountain]]s of the western [[Mediterranean region]], from southern [[France]] (including [[Corsica]]) across eastern and central [[Spain]] to [[Morocco]] and locally in northern [[Algeria]].<ref name=adams>Adams, R. P. (2004). ''Junipers of the World''. Trafford. {{ISBN|1-4120-4250-X}}</ref><ref name=farjon>Farjon, A. (2005). ''Monograph of Cupressaceae and Sciadopitys''. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. {{ISBN|1-84246-068-4}}</ref>

The name ''thurifera'' comes from the Latin ''turifer'', "producer/bearer of incense".<ref name=gd/>

It is a large [[shrub]] or [[tree]] reaching {{Convert|6–20|m|abbr=off}} tall, with a trunk up to {{Convert|2|m|ft|abbr=on|frac=2}} in diameter and a broadly conical to rounded or irregular crown. The foliage is strongly aromatic with a spicy-resinous scent. The [[leaves]] are of two forms: juvenile needle-like leaves {{Convert|8–10|mm|abbr=off|frac=16}} long on seedlings and irregularly on adult plants, and adult-scale leaves 0.6–3 mm long on older plants; they are arranged in decussate opposite pairs. It is [[plant sexuality|dioecious]] with separate male and female plants. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are berry-like, 7–12 mm in diameter, blue-black with a whitish waxy bloom, and contain 1–4 [[seed]]s; they are mature in about 18 months. The male cones are 3–4 mm long, and shed their pollen in early spring.<ref name=adams/><ref name=farjon/><ref name=montes>Ecology and conservation of ''Juniperus thurifera'' [http://n.montes.free.fr/uspage.html ''Juniperus thurifera'' website]</ref><ref name=gd>{{Gymnosperm Database|family=Cupressaceae|genus=Juniperus|species=thurifera}}</ref>

There are two [[Variety (botany)|varieties]], regarded as distinct by some authors,<ref name=adams/><ref name=montes/> but not by others:<ref name=farjon/>
*''Juniperus thurifera'' var. ''thurifera''. Spain, France. Mature cones 8–12 mm, with 2–4 seeds.
*''Juniperus thurifera'' var. ''africana'' Maire. Morocco, Algeria. Mature cones 7–8 mm, with 1–2 seeds.

Overall, the species is not considered threatened with healthy population in Spain;<ref name="iucn status 13 November 2021" /> however, the African population is threatened by severe [[overgrazing]], mainly by [[goat]]s, and is listed as Endangered.<ref name=adams/><ref name=montes/>

The largest Spanish Juniper forest in Europe is in the [[Sierra de Solorio]].<ref>[https://mundoarbol.blogspot.com/2011/03/arboles-de-espana-curiosidades-03-la.html El Sabinar más extenso de Europa]</ref>
